# kit-new rollback repair: final source review

Finding: no confirmed deletion blocker in the integrated two-file repair.

F1 (low, compatibility): main.go:475 uses Root.Open to acquire a read pin after creating a write-only descriptor. A process umask that removes owner-read permission, or an ACL that allows write but denies read, now makes scaffold fail and retain that output. A scratch POSIX probe with umask 0777 produced mode 000 and EACCES on read-open while the writer remained open. This is fail-closed, but prior scaffolding could finish. Accept and document the support limit, or qualify a permission-preserving alternative. It is not evidence of unsafe deletion.

Source path: main.go:339-417 registers pin-close before rollback, so LIFO cleanup runs while parent root and pins remain open. File pins are acquired at :475 while the writer is still open; Stat/SameFile verifies the original handle at :480-486. Root.Open and Root.OpenRoot are rooted APIs; Go 1.26 Windows Openat shares delete access, unlike ordinary os.Open. A workspace directory pin is acquired and verified at :438-451. Known pin/stat failures retain the unknown path. The writer close hook still runs at :500-509 before afterCreate, preserving write/close failure timing. Resource bound is five file pins, one workspace pin, parent root, and one active writer.

Rollback at main.go:354-399 checks name identity, original mode, live pin identity, regular-file type, exact reported write count, exact size, and bytes of the reported written prefix before removal. Invalid counts retain; a nil-error short write becomes io.ErrShortWrite. Each read pin starts at offset zero and is read only once in production. It can detect ordinary in-place byte or mode edits. It cannot detect a same-byte rewrite or close the Lstat-to-Remove namespace race, as the draft contract states.

Tests at main_test.go:478-653 cover same-byte and directory replacement, in-place edits, chmod, pin failures, invalid/short counts, and pin release. The original Linux-red test at :421-475 is unchanged. Worker-reported Mac race passed. My review used source and a small permission probe; I did not run a new gate or native Linux/Windows test. Fathom review_diff indexed 3e23005 and marked changed files stale, so it is impact context, not fresh proof. Require a green new Linux CI race run before closing the regression; Windows cross-build is compilation only.
